enhance_desc: Upload audio and a trained checkpoint to enhance it to 96kHz/24-bit.
enhance_tip: Tip: Use the Analyze tab to compare before/after quality metrics.
enhance_upload_audio: Upload an audio file to enhance.
enhance_upload_checkpoint: Upload a model checkpoint (.pt file) to enhance audio.
analyze_desc: Upload audio to see technical info, dynamics, spectrum, and perceptual quality metrics.
analyze_upload: Upload an audio file to analyze.
desc_peak_level: Loudest moment in the track. 0 dBFS = digital maximum. Typical: -1 to -0.1 dBFS for mastered music.
desc_rms_level: Average perceived loudness. Streaming targets: -14 LUFS (Spotify), -16 LUFS (Apple). Loudness war: above -8.
desc_crest_factor: Peak-to-RMS ratio. Higher = more transient punch. Typical: 10-18 dB (well mastered), 4-6 dB (crushed/loudness war).
desc_dynamic_range: Difference between loud and quiet sections. Typical: 12+ dB (classical/jazz), 8-12 dB (rock/pop), <6 dB (EDM/compressed).
desc_clipping: Samples at digital maximum. 0% = clean headroom, 0.01-0.1% = brief peaks (often acceptable), 0.1-0.5% = mildly clipped, >0.5% = significant clipping.
desc_max_consecutive_clips: Consecutive clipped samples indicate hard limiting/brick-wall clipping. 0 = clean, 1-3 = intersample peaks, 4+ = audible distortion.
desc_stereo_width: Side-to-mid energy ratio. 0 = mono, 0.1-0.3 = typical mix, >0.5 = very wide/spatial.
desc_lr_correlation: How similar L and R channels are. Typical: 0.5-0.9. Near 1.0 = mono. Below 0.3 = possible phase issues.
desc_spectral_centroid: "Center of gravity" of the frequency spectrum. Typical: 1000-3000 Hz (pop/rock), 500-1500 Hz (bass-heavy), 3000+ Hz (bright/electronic).
desc_spectral_bandwidth: Spread of frequencies present. Typical: 2000-4000 Hz. Higher = richer harmonics and more complex arrangement.
desc_spectral_rolloff: Frequency below which 95% of energy sits. Typical: 8-15 kHz (MP3/compressed), 16-20 kHz (CD), 20+ kHz (hi-res).
desc_nyquist: Maximum representable frequency at this sample rate (sample_rate / 2).
desc_production_quality: Clarity, fidelity, frequency balance, and spatial imaging. Typical: 4-6 (amateur), 6-8 (professional), 8+ (studio master).
desc_enjoyment: How pleasant and engaging the music feels. Typical: 3-5 (background), 5-7 (good), 7+ (highly engaging).
desc_complexity: Arrangement complexity: layers, instruments, rhythmic variation. Typical: 2-4 (simple), 5-7 (full band), 7+ (orchestral/dense).
desc_usefulness: How well-suited for professional use (sync, broadcast). Typical: 3-5 (lo-fi/demo), 6-8 (broadcast ready), 8+ (premium).
desc_si_snr: How closely the signal matches the reference, ignoring volume. Typical: 15-25 dB (good), 25+ dB (transparent), <10 dB (significant artifacts).
desc_sdr: Overall signal quality vs distortion. Typical: 15-25 dB (good enhancement), 25+ dB (near-transparent), <10 dB (heavy processing).
desc_chroma: Are the notes and harmonies preserved? Typical: >0.98 (transparent), 0.90-0.98 (minor coloring), <0.90 (pitch/harmony damage).
desc_mfcc: Does the "character" of instruments sound the same? Typical: >0.95 (transparent), 0.85-0.95 (subtle EQ), <0.85 (tonal shift).
desc_onset_f1: Are the beats and note attacks in the right place? Typical: >0.95 (transparent), 0.85-0.95 (slight smear), <0.85 (timing damage).
desc_stft_loss: Frequency-domain accuracy across multiple time-frequency resolutions. Lower = closer match.
desc_mel_loss: Perceptually-weighted spectral difference using mel scale (mimics human hearing). Lower = better.
desc_perceptual_stft: A-weighted, mel-scaled STFT. Penalizes artifacts in the 2-5kHz sensitivity range.
desc_dynamics_loss: Crest factor + loudness matching. Ensures punch and DR are preserved.
desc_encodec: Neural perceptual distance in Meta's learned audio space. Captures timbre + texture.
desc_mastering_total: Combined mastering loss (all above weighted and summed).
desc_genre: Zero-shot genre classification via CLAP text-audio similarity. Top 5 genres with confidence.
desc_mood: Zero-shot mood/emotion classification via CLAP. Detects the emotional character of the music.
desc_instruments: Detected instruments via CLAP zero-shot prompts. Shows instruments with >5% confidence.
desc_key: Detected musical key and scale (major/minor) via Essentia's key extraction algorithm.
desc_bpm: Estimated tempo in beats per minute. Typical: 60-80 (ballad), 100-130 (pop/rock), 130-160 (dance/EDM).
desc_upscale_score: Overall upscale potential on a 0-100 scale. Higher = more quality improvement expected from super-resolution.
desc_effective_sr: The highest frequency actually present in the file, expressed as an equivalent sample rate. May be far below the nominal sample rate for lossy files.
desc_bandwidth_utilization: Fraction of the available frequency bandwidth that contains real signal energy. Low utilization suggests the file was encoded at a lower sample rate or passed through lossy compression.
desc_codec_artifacts: Signs of lossy compression: sharp spectral cutoff, pre-echo, spectral holes. Detected = likely MP3/AAC/OGG origin.
desc_effective_bit_depth: Estimated actual bit depth based on noise floor analysis. A 16-bit file stored in a 24-bit container still has 16-bit dynamic range.
desc_headroom_db: Available dynamic headroom before digital clipping. Calculated from declared bit depth: 16-bit ≈ 96 dB, 24-bit ≈ 144 dB.
desc_gap_ratio: Fraction of the spectrum between the spectral rolloff and the Nyquist frequency that contains no real signal. A large gap (>40%) strongly suggests lossy encoding or artificial sample rate conversion.
desc_sr_headroom: Gap between current sample rate and 96kHz target. Larger gap = more potential for the model to add harmonics.
desc_spectral_ceiling: Highest frequency with actual content. If well below Nyquist, the file was likely downsampled or lossy-encoded.
desc_bit_depth_headroom: Current bit depth vs 24-bit target. 16-bit has ~96dB dynamic range, 24-bit has ~144dB.
desc_enhancement_verdict: Overall assessment of how much this file could benefit from enhancement.
verdict_high: High potential — significant quality improvement expected from super-resolution.
verdict_medium: Medium potential — some improvement possible, mainly in high-frequency detail.
verdict_low: Low potential — file is already high quality. Enhancement may add subtle detail.
verdict_none: Already optimal — file exceeds target quality. No enhancement needed.
summary_high: This file would benefit significantly from super-resolution. The model is expected to reconstruct substantial missing high-frequency content.
summary_medium: This file has moderate upscale potential. The model can add some high-frequency detail.
summary_low: This file is already fairly well-preserved. Enhancement may add subtle harmonic detail.
summary_none: This file is already at or above target quality. Super-resolution is unlikely to improve it.
desc_comparison: Side-by-side comparison of original and processed audio. Green = improved, Red = degraded.
